he:Kiddush Levanah:1.en: According to Kabbalah, do not sanctify the moon until after 7 days from the molad. Sanctify the moon in fine garments. Before the blessing, say:

he:Kiddush Levanah:3.en: Straighten your feet and look at the moon once before the blessing; when you begin the blessing, do not look at it at all.

he:Kiddush Levanah:7.en: Do this three times: jump three jumps and say from 'Boruch Oshecha' to here.

parts.text: סִמָּן טוֹב וּמַזָּל טוֹב יִהְיֶה לָֽנוּ וּלְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵל. אָמֵן:
בְּעָלְמָֽא דִּי בְרָֽא כִרְעוּתֵהּ וְיַמְלִֽיךְ מַלְכוּתֵֽהּ,
בַּעֲגָלָא וּבִזְמַֽן קָרִיב וְאִמְרֽוּ אָמֵֽן: יְהֵא שְׁמֵהּ רַבָּֽא מְבָרַֽךְ לְעָלַֽם וּלְעָלְמֵֽי עָלְמַיָּֽא. יִתְבָּרֵֽךְ,

he:Kiddush Levanah:23.en: And shake the fringes of the tallit katan.

he:Lulav:1.en: Take the lulav with the species. The three species of lulav (lulav, hadas, and arava) must be tied and bound together, with no string or adhesive separating them. When taking them, the spine of the lulav should face you; hold three hadasim (one on the right, one on the left, one in the middle leaning slightly right) and two aravot (one on the right, one on the left).

he:Lulav:2.en: Halachically, one should bless on the lulav after the Amidah and before Hallel. However, since the mitzvah is best performed in the sukkah, and one cannot leave the synagogue due to onlookers, the blessing is made in the morning before the Amidah while still in the sukkah.

he:Lulav:3.en: First take the lulav alone in the right hand and make the blessing. Then take the etrog in the left hand. At the point where the text says 'lulav, hadas, and arava', join the etrog with the lulav and shake in the six directions (Hei-Yud). For each direction, make three movements out and three movements in (three times out and in). On each 'in' movement, touch the end of the lulav and its species and the etrog to your chest. When shaking, ensure the top of the lulav does not touch the wall; leave space.

he:Lulav:4.en: The order of shaking: 1) South, 2) North, 3) East, 4) Up, 5) Down (do not invert the lulav; the 'out' movement is downward and the 'in' movement is upward, opposite of the 'up' direction), 6) West. (In all movements, the top of the lulav points upward, but the 'out' movement is toward the direction being shaken).

he:Lulav:5.en: During Hallel, perform the six-direction shaking four times: once at the beginning of Hodu, once at Ana HaShem Haoshi'a Na, once at the repetition of Ana HaShem Haoshi'a Na, and once at the end of Hodu.

he:Lulav:6.en: If one blessed on the lulav after the Amidah in the synagogue, shake only three times during Hallel: at the beginning and end of Hodu, and once at Ana (as stated in the Rama).

he:Lulav:8.en: On the first time one blesses on the lulav, also recite Shehecheyanu.

he:Hallel:1.en: These are the days when Hallel is recited in full: the first two days and nights of Pesach, the two days of Shavuot, the nine days of Sukkot, and the eight days of Chanukah. On days when Hallel is not recited in full, the custom is that the chazzan recites the blessings at the beginning and end, and the congregation answers Amen, thereby fulfilling the obligation through his blessing.

he:Hallel:5.en: On Rosh Chodesh and Chol HaMoed Pesach, skip the following psalm.

he:Hallel:8.en: On Rosh Chodesh and Chol HaMoed Pesach, skip the following psalm.

parts.text: מִן־הַמֵּצַר קָרָֽאתִי יָהּ עָנָֽנִי בַמֶּרְחָב יָהּ: יְיָ לִי לֹא אִירָא מַה־יַּעֲשֶׂה לִי אָדָם: יְיָ לִי בְּעֹזְרָי וַאֲנִי אֶרְאֶה בְשׂנְאָי: טוֹב לַחֲסוֹת בַּייָ מִבְּטֹֽחַ בָּאָדָם: טוֹב לַחֲסוֹת בַּייָ מִבְּטֹֽחַ בִּנְדִיבִים: כָּל־גּוֹיִם סְבָבֽוּנִי בְּשֵׁם יְיָ כִּי אֲמִילַם: סַבּֽוּנִי גַם־סְבָבֽוּנִי בְּשֵׁם יְיָ כִּי אֲמִילַם: סַבּֽוּנִי כִדְבֹרִים דֹּעֲכוּ כְּאֵשׁ קוֹצִים בְּשֵׁם יְיָ כִּי אֲמִילַם: דָּחֹה דְחִיתַֽנִי לִנְפֹּל וַייָ עֲזָרָֽנִי: עָזִּי וְזִמְרָת יָהּ וַיְהִי־לִי לִישׁוּעָה: קוֹל רִנָּה וִישׁוּעָה בְּאָהֳלֵי צַדִּיקִים יְמִין יְיָ עֹֽשָׂה חָֽיִל: יְמִין יְיָ רוֹמֵמָה יְמִין יְיָ עֹֽשָׂה חָֽיִל: לֹא־אָמוּת כִּי־אֶחְיֶה וַאֲסַפֵּר מַעֲשֵׂי יָהּ: יַסֹּר יִסְּרַֽנִּי יָהּ וְלַמָּֽוֶת לֹא נְתָנָֽנִי: פִּתְחוּ־לִי שַֽׁעֲרֵי־צֶֽדֶק אָֽבֹא־בָם אוֹדֶה יָהּ: זֶה־הַשַּֽׁעַר לַייָ צַדִּיקִים יָבֹֽאוּ בוֹ: אוֹדְךָ כִּי עֲנִיתָֽנִי וַתְּהִי־לִי לִישׁוּעָה:
אֶֽבֶן מָאֲסוּ הַבּוֹנִים הָיְתָה לְרֹאשׁ פִּנָּה:
מֵאֵת יְיָ הָֽיְתָה זֹּאת הִיא נִפְלָאת בְּעֵינֵֽינוּ:
זֶה־הַיּוֹם עָשָׂה יְיָ נָגִֽילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָה בוֹ:
בָּרוּךְ הַבָּא בְּשֵׁם יְיָ בֵּרַכְנוּכֶם מִבֵּית יְיָ:
אֵל יְיָ וַיָּֽאֶר לָֽנוּ אִסְרוּ־חַג בַּעֲבֹתִים עַד־קַרְנוֹת הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ:
הוֹדוּ לַייָ כִּי־טוֹב כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ:
וְיַקְדִּֽישׁוּ וְיַמְלִֽיכוּ אֶת שִׁמְךָ מַלְכֵּֽנוּ. כִּי לְךָ טוֹב לְהוֹדוֹת,
כִּי מֵעוֹלָם וְעַד עוֹלָם אַתָּה אֵל. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ,

he:Hallel:26.en: On Rosh Chodesh, Yom Tov, and Chol HaMoed, recite Kaddish Shalem; on Chanukah, recite Half Kaddish.

he:Hallel:27.en: On Rosh Chodesh, Yom Tov, and Chol HaMoed, recite the Psalm of the Day here. On Rosh Chodesh, recite Barchi Nafshi after the Psalm of the Day, followed by Kaddish d'Rabbanan.

he:Hallel:28.en: The Torah is taken out and four men are called up on Rosh Chodesh and Chol HaMoed. Kaddish is recited over the Torah. Then Ashrei and Uva LeTziyon are recited, and the Torah is returned to the Ark. Afterwards, the chazzan recites Half Kaddish, and the Musaf prayer is recited. Tefillin are removed on Rosh Chodesh before the Kaddish. On Chanukah, three men are called up, followed by Kaddish, Ashrei, Uva LeTziyon, and Kaddish Shalem. The Torah is returned to the Ark, and then 'Beit Yaakov' is recited.

he:Annulment of Vows:1.en: It is explained in the Talmud and codes that annulment applies only to vows and oaths concerning oneself (e.g., eating or sleeping). Vows made to others or to any person of any nation/religion cannot be annulled.

he:Annulment of Vows:2.en: On Erev Rosh Hashanah before midnight. It is best to have a complete court of three:

he:Kapparot:1.en: On Erev Yom Kippur it is customary to slaughter a white rooster called 'Gever' (male) and a hen for a woman, in the morning watch after Selichot, when the thread of kindness prevails. We slaughter it to subdue the forces of judgment and draw out its blood to sweeten them. This is called 'Kapparah' (atonement), like the scapegoat. The number of birds should match the number of people in the house: a male for a male, a female for a female. For a pregnant woman, slaughter three: one for her, and a male and female for the uncertain sex of the child.

לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּרִית עוֹלָם: וְנֶאֱמַר וַיָּמָל אַבְרָהָם אֶת יִצְחָק בְּנוֹ בֶּן שְׁמוֹנַת יָמִים,
כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה אֹתוֹ אֱלֺהִים: הוֹדוּ לַיהוָֹה כִּי טוֹב,
כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ: הוֹדוּ לַיהוָֹה כִּי טוֹב,
כֵּן יִכָּנֵס לְתוֹרָה וּלְחֻפָּה וּלְמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים:

he:Order of a Circumcision:14.en: They give the infant to drink from the cup of blessing, or he drinks it himself. After the circumcision, the mohel and the father pray this prayer:

parts.text: כְּאִלּוּ הִקְרַבְתִּֽיהוּ לִפְנֵי כִסֵּא כְבוֹדֶֽךָ. וְאַתָּה בְּרַחֲמֶֽיךָ הָרַבִּים,
שְׁלַח עַל־יְדֵי מַלְאָכֶֽיךָ הַקְּדוֹשִׁים נְשָׁמָה קְדוֹשָׁה וּטְהוֹרָה (
וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה לִבּוֹ פָתֽוּחַ כְּפִתְחוֹ שֶׁל אוּלָם בְּתוֹרָתְךָ הַקְּדוֹשָׁה,
מִי שֶׁבֵּרַךְ אֲבוֹתֵינוּ אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב משֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן דָּוִד וּשְׁלֹמֹה הוּא יְבָרֵךְ אֶת־הַיֶּֽלֶד הָרַךְ הַנִּימוֹל (

) יִתֵּן בְּלִי נֶדֶר עֲבוּרוֹ לִצְדָקָה לְבִקּוּר חוֹלִים בִּשְׂכַר זֶה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יִשְׁלַח לוֹ מְהֵרָה רְפוּאָה שְׁלֵמָה בְּכָל רמ״ח אֵבָרָיו ושסה גִּידָיו וִיגַּדְּלֻהוּ לְתוֹרָה וּלְחֻפָּה וּלְמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים,

he:Chanukah:1.en: Bless before lighting each night: 'Blessed... to kindle the Chanukah light' and 'Who performed miracles'. On the first night, also bless 'Who has kept us alive'. Do not light until all blessings are finished. The proper custom is to attach the candles or hang the menorah on the doorpost thickness, in the doorway. On the first night, start lighting from the right candle; from the second night onward, bless on the added candle and proceed from left to right.

he:Purim:1.en: One is obligated to read the Megillah at night and repeat it during the day. The Megillah must be unfolded like a letter. Three blessings are recited over it. Shehecheyanu is recited only at night, not during the day. It is customary to recite Kaddish Shalem after the Amidah before reading the Megillah at night:

he:Purim:5.en: When reading the Megillah in public, the following blessing is recited afterwards [Baruch... HaRav et Rivenu...], but not when reading alone:

he:Purim:8.en: After reading the Megillah at night, recite VeAtah Kadosh (and if it falls on Motzaei Shabbat, recite Vihi Noam and VeAtah Kadosh), followed by Kaddish without Titkabal:

he:Purim:9.en: During the day, after reading the Megillah, recite Ashrei and UVa LeTziyon, followed by Kaddish Shalem. Before reading the Torah and the Megillah, after the Amidah, only Half Kaddish is recited:
